target: Ball–Simoens Problem 16, smallest open case n=7: is every set of 4 mutually orthogonal quantum Latin squares of order 7 classical (equivalently M(7) <= 3)?

definitions.QLS: n×n array of vectors of C^n; every row and every column is an orthonormal basis.
definitions.orthogonal: Two QLS (psi_ij), (phi_ij) are orthogonal if {psi_ij ⊗ phi_ij} is an orthonormal basis of C^n ⊗ C^n.
definitions.set_isotopy: phase factors on entries; simultaneous row and column permutations of all squares; a separate unitary applied to all entries of each square.
definitions.classical: A set is classical if, up to isotopy, all entries lie in a fixed orthonormal basis {|1>,...,|n>}.
definitions.M(n): largest t such that a non-classical set of t MOQLS(n) exists (0 if none).
definitions.parent_note: Because the unitary in isotopy acts per square and permutations do not alter which rays occur, a set is classical iff each square is classical up to its own unitary [INFERENCE: re-derive in the lane before use].

primary_attestation.source: Ball, Simoens, Large sets of mutually orthogonal quantum Latin squares, arXiv:2607.12933v2
quotes: Problem 16. Is a set of n − 3 MOQLS(n), n ̸= 4, necessarily classical?
Theorem 5. Suppose n ≥ 3. A set of n − 2 MOQLS(n) is classical. Thus, M (n) ≤ n − 3.
Table 2: New bounds on M (n) for 2 ≤ n ≤ 17. [n=7: 2-4]
primary_attestation.location: layout text lines 28-80 (Problem 1, Theorems 2-5, Table 2), 173-230 (proof of Theorem 5), 392-401 (Problems 16-17); parent read all
primary_attestation.why_smallest: For n=5 and n=6, n−3 = 2 and 3 already exceed the known M(5)=M(6)=1 (Theorem 4.2: non-classical pairs exist iff n >= 7); n=4 is excluded in the problem. So n=7 is the smallest open instance.

baseline: M(7) ∈ {2,3,4}: lower bound from Corollary 7 / Huang–Li; upper bound from Theorem 5. Theorem 5 proof: rules #1-#3 force weight <= 2 for n−2 squares, then Lemma 10 and Theorem 9 (Shrikhande extension of n−3 MOLS to n−1 for n != 4). For 4 MOQLS(7) the same rules only give weight <= 3 [INFERENCE: re-derive].

acceptance.positive_answer: Complete proof that every set of 4 MOQLS(7) is classical. Computer assistance allowed only with exact or rigorously certified computation, a stated proof that the finite search is exhaustive (pattern rules, symmetry reductions), and two independent implementations for any exhaustive step.
acceptance.negative_answer: Explicit non-classical set of 4 MOQLS(7) with exact algebraic entries (e.g. cyclotomic), verified by two independent exact checkers: rows/columns orthonormal, pairwise tensor-product orthonormal bases, and an isotopy-invariant non-classicality certificate (e.g. more than 7 distinct rays among one square's entries).
acceptance.partial: A proof that weight-3 entries cannot occur, or a complete reduction to stated finite cases, is a reportable intermediate lemma, not the theorem.

controls: Theorem 5 must be reproduced for 5 MOQLS(7) (classical); a Corollary 7 / Huang–Li non-classical pair of order 7 must be certified non-classical by the same invariant; the classical complete set of 6 MOLS(7) must pass as classical; mutation controls for every checker.
